Drive-time cartogram map

Source: R/cartogram_map.R
mysterymaps_cartogram_map.Rd

Redraws each polygon scaled radially around its nearest hub (e.g. a provider or partner site), so areas whose real drive time is far out of proportion to their straight-line distance balloon outward, and well-connected areas pull inward. This is not a true-area map – it deliberately distorts geography to encode travel time instead.

Usage

mysterymaps_cartogram_map(
  polygons,
  hub_id_var,
  hub_lon_var,
  hub_lat_var,
  time_var,
  straight_distance_var,
  distance_unit = "miles",
  scale_clip = c(0.2, 3),
  hub_points = NULL,
  hub_label = "Site",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  reference_minutes = 30
)

Arguments

polygons

sf polygon layer, one row per area to warp.

hub_id_var

character(1): column in polygons identifying the polygon (joined to hub_lon_var/hub_lat_var/time_var/ straight_distance_var, all also columns of polygons, one value per row).

hub_lon_var, hub_lat_var

character(1): numeric columns in polygons giving each row's hub longitude/latitude (WGS84).

time_var

character(1): numeric column, drive time in minutes from each polygon to its hub.

straight_distance_var

character(1): numeric column, straight-line distance from each polygon to its hub, in the unit named by distance_unit.

distance_unit

character(1): unit of straight_distance_var, one of "miles" (default) or "kilometers". Only used to label the drive- time reference line; the warp math itself is unit-agnostic as long as straight_distance_var is consistent.

scale_clip

Length-2 numeric: c(min, max) bounds on the per-row warp scale factor. Default c(0.2, 3).

hub_points, hub_label

Optional sf POINT layer of the hubs themselves (e.g. provider locations), warped the same way and drawn on top, with its own hub_time_var/hub_straight_distance_var columns (minutes/distance from each hub to itself, i.e. 0, OR from each named target site to its nearest hub – see examples in package tests). NULL omits.

title, subtitle, caption

Character labels. NULL omits.

reference_minutes

numeric(1): length, in minutes of typical-pace travel, of the drawn reference line. Default 30.

Value

A ggplot object. The caller saves it; this function writes nothing.

Details

A straight-line distance near zero (the hub essentially inside the polygon) makes the warp ratio time / distance blow up into a meaningless value that has nothing to do with genuine circuitousness – it is purely an artifact of dividing by a near-zero denominator. Per-row scale factors are clipped to scale_clip (default c(0.2, 3)) for exactly this reason: without the clip, a handful of near-zero-distance polygons would misleadingly read as "the most distorted" on the map.

The calibration constant (how much distance one minute of drive time "should" correspond to, in the undistorted/typical-pace case) is derived automatically from the data: median(straight_distance_var) / median(time_var) across all rows with both values present. A polygon whose warp ratio is near this median pace is drawn close to its true shape and position; a polygon far slower or faster than that pace is pushed out or pulled in accordingly.

A real distance scale bar would misrepresent this map, since distance on it deliberately does not mean distance – this function draws a "drive time scale" reference line instead, equal to reference_minutes of typical-pace travel, rather than calling mysterymaps_scale_bar().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
counties <- sf::st_sf(
  id = 1:4,
  hub_lon = -97.5, hub_lat = 40.5,
  time_min = c(10, 20, 30, 60),
  straight_miles = c(9.6, 19.2, 28.8, 57.6),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(lapply(1:4, function(i) {
    x <- -100 + i
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(x, x + 1, x + 1, x, x), c(40, 40, 41, 41, 40))))
  }), crs = 4326)
)
mysterymaps_cartogram_map(
  counties, hub_id_var = "id", hub_lon_var = "hub_lon", hub_lat_var = "hub_lat",
  time_var = "time_min", straight_distance_var = "straight_miles")
}
